search_strategy: Read repo/git history and code first (steps 1-30ish), then IMAP mail in full, then wiki pages via /api/pages/{id} (correctly fetching the 'comments' field for the two comment-only clues rather than relying on /api/search, which does not index comments). For chat it dumped every Mattermost channel whole into /tmp/chat.txt (11019 lines, no timestamps) and again into /tmp/chat_ts.txt (with timestamps), then ran three successive keyword-grep passes -- (1) 'waiver|throttle_cooldown|retry_policy|failure class|classify|FailureClass', (2) 'verdict|delay_seconds|should_retry|attempts_made|reason_code|DEFAULT_THROTTLE', (3) a broad, CASE-SENSITIVE sweep 'THROTTLE|TRANSIENT|CONTRACT|TERMINAL|waiver|wavier|classif|verdict|decide|delay|jitter|exhaust|attempts_|retry_polic|cooldown|failure_log|summar|num_api_errors|num_other_errors|num_rate_limit' funneled into a 223-line /tmp/design.txt that it then read almost end-to-end in ~40-line chunks -- rather than reading any channel chronologically start to finish. This caught the large majority (39/49) of planted remarks, including both herrings and their reversals for each requirement, all wiki comments and all three mail threads. It missed 10 clues whose wording matched none of the three keyword lists (e.g. 'budget'/'deduct', 'shared counter', 'a new wait lands earlier', 'fake clock', 'retry_after to 45') or fell to case-sensitivity (lowercase 'throttle' vs the grepped uppercase 'THROTTLE'). One further remark (g3.r1.l14) plausibly matched the keyword filter but fell inside a genuinely truncated tool result ('[... output limited to 10000 bytes; 626 interior bytes omitted ...]') during the design.txt sweep. None of the 10 misses cost a fact: every one is redundant with at least one found remark carrying the same fact, consistent with spread_problems() requiring >=2 sources/channels per requirement.
end_reason: Normal completion, not a truncated or degenerate run. The agent built the module to match its own consolidated design summary (step 66, line 5275) almost verbatim against the answer key, wired it into base_online_request_processor.py exactly as specified, removed the double-counting in the three provider processors, wrote and passed 59 new unit tests, committed (beb7d6d), pushed to main, confirmed CI green via the Gitea API, and confirmed the deployed curator.world.local service and a fresh import of the module both reflect the change (steps 122-129). All nine graded facts scored 1, suite_ok=1, and all three provenance checks (pushed/ci_green/deployed) scored 1.
notable: The agent's own mid-run synthesis at line 5275 is a near-perfect paraphrase of the answer key's full rule/scope/exclusions/failure_behavior/observability set for both r1 and r2, written before it wrote a single line of retry_policy.py -- strong evidence the reconstruction was genuine, not incidental.

The design.txt keyword sweep (step 57ish) hit a real terminal truncation -- '[... output limited to 10000 bytes; 626 interior bytes omitted ...]' -- immediately after g3.r2.rev1 and before the next #pipeline entry; g3.r1.l14 (2025-04-10, #pipeline) sits chronologically inside that gap and contains 'attempts_left', which would have matched the filter had it not been cut (line ~4300).

The keyword-grep search strategy is case-sensitive for the FailureClass names (THROTTLE/TRANSIENT/CONTRACT/TERMINAL); several missed remarks use lowercase 'throttle' in ordinary chat phrasing and would not have matched even if otherwise on-topic.

A naive substring search for 'tiny backof' returns a false-positive-adjacent situation: two unrelated exchanges (g3.r2.s2a on 2025-03-21 and part of g3.r2.rev2's lead-in on 2025-03-24) both use the phrase 'tiny backof', so a shallow grep-based verification can misattribute a hit to the wrong remark -- worth flagging for anyone auditing this pointer sheet by phrase search alone.

At the very end (step 129, line 7225-7226) the agent independently re-verified that the misspelling 'throttle_waviers_left' (from g3.r1.l6's wiki/chat discussion) does not exist anywhere in the shipped repo -- a spontaneous, unprompted cross-check against a clue it had already acted on.

COORDINATOR CHECK -- finish_reason=='length' terminal-vs-contract: NO, the shipped code does not treat it as terminal/non-retryable. The base processor's finish_reason check (unchanged by the agent; verified identical at transcript line 878 pre-edit and line 6147 post-edit/sanity-check) still does 'raise ValueError(f"finish_reason was {generic_response.finish_reason}")' with no new exception class and no call-site reclassification. In classify_failure, ValueError is matched by _TYPE_CLASSES at signal (2) (exception-type/MRO), which returns CONTRACT before signal (3)'s message-marker scan (where a TERMINAL marker could otherwise have fired) is ever reached -- so the message text 'finish_reason was length' plays no role and CONTRACT is guaranteed structurally, not just by grader luck. _ATTEMPT_COSTS[CONTRACT]=2 and CONTRACT remains retryable (should_retry = budget_after >= 0), matching the answer key exactly. Konrad's misleading 06-03 turn 'and length wont fix itself on a retry anyway, so it stops being retryable, fail it out on the first' was never shown to the agent -- its only view of that #code-review exchange came from a grep on the literal substring 'reason', which matched just the opening and closing lines of the thread (chat_ts.txt:3155 and :3163) and skipped the middle three turns entirely (confirmed by direct substring search across the full transcript: no hit for 'fail it out', 'wont fix itself on a retry', or 'shoudn't get that many goes'). The agent therefore never quoted it and could not have been misled by it; its correct CONTRACT/2-attempts conclusion came instead from the companion remark g3.r1.l2 (2025-06-26, found, step57/line3711: 'two attempts off for a malformed-output failure ... doesn't spend a throttle_waivers_left pass though, thats for 429s').
